thread.title: Nokia CEO Suri: Telecom is Being Gobbled by Cloud Operators

author: Tiernan Ray
title: Nokia CEO Suri: Telecom is Being Gobbled by Cloud Operators
text:
Nokia CEO Rajeev Suri addressing press and media at the start of the Mobile World Congress in Barcelona. / CREDIT: Tiernan Ray for Barron's. The most intriguing bit from Nokia ( NOK ) chief executive Rajeev Suri at the Mobile World Congress trade show on Sunday in Barcelona was that the old networks of the telecommunications operators are increasingly seeing their traffic sucked away by the cloud computing operators, companies such as Alphabet ’s ( GOOGL ) Google and Amazon ( AMZN ), and even Apple ( AAPL ).
“More and more traffic in the backbone of the Internet will be in the networks of web-scale companies, the Apple’s, Googles, Alibabas, Tencents, and others of the world."
"This is already under way and will only accelerate in the coming years."
“The growth in data center to data center traffic is going to outstrip” the growth of mobile data, he said. “What is happening is that traffic is moving off service provider networks and nearer to the end user, and it is then moving onto the big backbone network of web-scale players."
“This is a fundamental change,” he said.
Much of the talk was an update on progress in “ 5G ,” the new broadband standard that is set to take over today’s existing cellular data networks.
Suri said things are proceeding faster than expected. “We expect 5G adoption to be more rapid than what we saw in earlier generations of technology, pretty much across all countries."
“It is coming really fast.”
Consensus in the market last year was the first 5G capable devices would become available in volumes, and 3GPP compatible networks would become available in 2019."
“Scratch that: Customer interest has accelerated, and the market has accelerated.”
“Commercial 5G networks will launch, maybe as early as the end of this year, or early 2019. It is quite remarkable. Even eight months ago many operators I talked to shrugged off 5G. Now they get it, and the race is on."
To hammer home the point, he announced that Nokia had, just three hours prior to the press conference, signed a memorandum of understanding with China Mobile ( CHL ) to work on 5G.
Suri described a “neck and neck race” between the U.S. and China, “pretty much ahead of the rest of the world."
Korea and Japan and other countries are also moving swiftly, but Suri said Europe was lagging and would continued to do so, because there are too many operators, lacking consolidation, and there is too much regulation in Europe.”
Also in the talk, Suri promoted new WiFi router products from Nokia, calling the slick white canisters “beautiful,” in contrast to what he labeled the ugly black boxes that exist today.
He also talked up a partnership with Facebook ( FB ) to put wireless access devices using 60-gigahertz spectrum on lamp-posts in neighborhoods, creating high-speed broadband “mesh networks."
You can watch the entire presentation on Nokia’s Web site .
Suri with the company's WiFi appliance.
